questions.question: Which French chemist summarised his experiment in 1806, and proved that the mass ratio of elements in a chemical compound is always the same, regardless of the source of the compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joseph Proust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joseph Louis Proust **was a French chemist. He was best known for his discovery of the law of definite proportions in **1794**, stating that chemical compounds always combine in constant proportions.
 
• The **law of** **definite proportions** dictates that a name is always associated with a specific ratio of elements found in a chemical compound**.**
 
• If the** ratio of elements** is different from that specific** **ratio then it is not the same compound and therefor has a different name.
 
• The law of constant proportion was given b **Joseph Proust** in **1797**.
 
• This observation was first made by the English theologian and chemist **Joseph Priestley** and **Antoine Lavoisier** , a French nobleman and chemist centered on the process of combustion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Using the** law of definite proportions**, the composition of compounds will always be the same by mass.
 
• In Chemistry, **stoichiometry** is based on this law.
 
 
• **Statement:**__ Chemical compounds consist of elements that are always present at fixed ratios (in terms of their mass) according to the law of definite proportions as well as the law of constant proportions. In this ratio, neither the source nor the method of preparation of the chemical compound is relevant.
 
• __**Explanation:**__ Chemical compounds, according to the law of constant proportions, are made of elements present in a fixed ratio by mass. The concentration of each element in a compound will always be the same by mass regardless of the source of the sample.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen **and **oxygen **atoms are always in a** 1:2 **ratio in the nitrogen dioxide molecule (NO2).
 
• Consequently,** Nitrogen** has the **same structure as oxygen**.

questions.question: In which year did Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulate his famous aphorism 'Omnis cellula - e cellula' which became a part of the foundation of cell theory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1855**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow** formulated his famous aphorism **"Omnis cellula - e cellula"** in **1855**. 
 
• This statement, which translates to "Every cell originates from another existing cell like it," became a foundational concept in the development of the cell theory, emphasizing the continuity of cellular life and the principle that cells arise only from pre-existing cells. 
 
• German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician Rudolf Ludwig Carl Virchow was born in 1896.
 
• In addition to being the creator of social medicine and referred to by his peers as the "Pope of medicine," he is recognized as "the father of modern pathology." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The cell theory, **established in the mid-19th century, revolutionized biology by providing a unifying framework for understanding life. 
 
• It asserts that all living organisms are composed of cells, which are the basic structural and functional units of life. 
 
• Furthermore, cells are the fundamental building blocks of all organisms, and new cells arise only from pre-existing cells through cell division. 
 
• This theory laid the foundation for modern biology, guiding research and shaping our understanding of cellular processes and the complexities of life itself.

questions.question: When was Kapil Dev awarded with Padma Shri Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kapil Dev,** an iconic figure in Indian cricket, was honored with the** Padma Shri in 1982** and the **Padma Bhushan in 1991**, two of** India's highest civilian awards**. 
 
• He was named the Indian Cricketer of the Century in 2002 and inducted into the International Cricket Council's Hall of Fame in 2010, recognizing his exceptional contributions to the sport. 
 
• Kapil Dev Nikhanj, an esteemed former Indian cricketer, is renowned as one of the finest all-rounders in cricket history, excelling as a fast-medium bowler and a powerful middle-order batsman.
 
• He holds the unique distinction of being the only player to have amassed over 400 wickets (434 wickets) and scored more than 5,000 runs in Test matches.
 
• As captain, Dev led the Indian cricket team to victory in the 1983 Cricket World Cup, making history as the first Indian captain to achieve this milestone. Notably, he remains the youngest captain, having achieved this feat at the age of 24.
 
• Retiring in 1994, he was the first player to claim 200 wickets in One Day Internationals (ODIs) and held the world record for the highest number of wickets in Test cricket until it was surpassed by Courtney Walsh in 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Padma Shri **stands as the fourth-highest civilian award in India, following the Bharat Ratna, the Padma Vibhushan, and the Padma Bhushan. 
 
• Established on January 2, 1954, this accolade is bestowed in acknowledgment of outstanding contributions across a wide array of fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, acting, medicine, social service, and public affairs. 
 
• Annually conferred by the Government of India, it is a prestigious honor awarded on India's Republic Day.
